definitions.rationale: This is the first equation of the named contribution summary, defining the square contribution when the index is divisible by three.
definitions.text:
rule contribution(I:Int, X:Int) => X *Int X
    requires pyMod(I, 3) ==Int 0

definitions.rationale: This is the second piecewise equation of contribution, defining the cube case when divisibility by four holds and the earlier divisibility-by-three case does not.
definitions.text:
rule contribution(I:Int, X:Int) => X *Int X *Int X
    requires pyMod(I, 3) =/=Int 0 andBool pyMod(I, 4) ==Int 0

definitions.rationale: This is the final piecewise equation of contribution, defining the unchanged-value case when neither earlier branch applies.
definitions.text:
rule contribution(I:Int, X:Int) => X
    requires pyMod(I, 3) =/=Int 0 andBool pyMod(I, 4) =/=Int 0

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the base case of the tail-recursive sumSquares mathematical summary: an empty remainder returns the accumulator.
This recurrence defines sumSquares on a nonempty integer sequence by advancing the index and adding the head's defined contribution.
definitions.text:
rule sumSquares(intCons(X:Int, XS:Ints), I:Int, ACC:Int)
    => sumSquares(XS, I +Int 1, ACC +Int contribution(I, X))

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the empty-sequence base case of the endIndex structural summary.
This recurrence defines endIndex for a nonempty remainder by consuming one element and incrementing the index.
definitions.text:
rule endIndex(intCons(_:Int, XS:Ints), I:Int)
    => endIndex(XS, I +Int 1)

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the empty-sequence base case of endValue, preserving the previously bound value.
This recurrence defines endValue on a nonempty remainder by carrying the current head forward as the most recently bound value.
This macro-expansion rule defines the named proof term sumSquaresLoopBody as the exact translated loop-body statement sequence.
definitions.text:
rule sumSquaresLoopBody
    => If(
         Compare(
           BinOp("%", Name("index"), Int(3)),
           CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
         AugAssign(
           Name("total"),
           "+",
           BinOp("*", Name("value"), Name("value")))
         .Stmts,
         If(
           Compare(
             BinOp("%", Name("index"), Int(4)),
             CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
           AugAssign(
             Name("total"),
             "+",
             BinOp(
               "*",
               BinOp("*", Name("value"), Name("value")),
               Name("value")))
           .Stmts,
           AugAssign(Name("total"), "+", Name("value"))
           .Stmts)
         .Stmts)
       AugAssign(Name("index"), "+", Int(1))
       .Stmts

definitions.rationale: This macro-expansion rule defines the named proof term sumSquaresFunctionBody as the initialization, loop, and return statement sequence.
definitions.text:
rule sumSquaresFunctionBody
    => Assign(Name("total"), Int(0))
       Assign(Name("index"), Int(0))
       For(Name("value"), Name("lst"), sumSquaresLoopBody)
       Return(Name("total"))
       .Stmts

operational_rules.rationale: This k-cell rule implements the iterator observation for the empty symbolic integer-list representation by producing #iterDone; it is execution behavior in the verification model, not an additional mathematical fact.
This k-cell rule implements one iterator step for a nonempty symbolic integer list, yielding its head and residual iterator; it is ordinary operational behavior of the verification model.
